Overview.Name: Dinesh Kumar Peruri
Overview.Goal: Support fat loss and stabilise blood sugar through clean, protein-focused meals that reduce overeating triggers and remove fried or spicy foods for appearance, energy, confidence, and preventing health issues.

Meal_1_Brunch: 3 whole eggs pan fried in ghee
OR 150–180g chicken cooked in ghee with mild seasoning
OR One bowl cooked vegetables such as bottle gourd, ridge gourd, carrots, beans
OR One small fruit like apple or orange
Meal_2_Dinner: 150–180g paneer or chicken cooked in ghee
OR Small portion rice if needed for energy
Snack_Optional_If_Hungry: OR Puffed rice with onion and lemon

Notes_and_Tips: Diabetes responds well to steady protein intake and minimal processed carbs. Keep your two meals rich in eggs, paneer, and chicken.
Since fried and spicy foods trigger cravings, avoid hotel food, deep-fried items, and masala-heavy dishes. Use only ghee, pepper, rock salt, ginger, garlic, turmeric, and herbs.
Stress and late nights increase hunger. Pause before eating, drink warm water, or take a short walk to reduce stress-driven eating.
Walk 10 minutes after each meal to help blood sugar stay stable.
Sleep and irregular work hours can increase cravings. Maintain consistent meal timing to reduce blood sugar swings.
Increase daily steps to 6k–7k over the next few weeks. Even slow walking helps fat loss in diabetes.
Keep meals repetitive if needed. Simple protein-and-vegetable plates give better control than variety that leads to overeating.
If you feel low energy, increase protein, not carbs for better blood sugar management.
Keep flavours simple and low spice to avoid sugar spikes and craving triggers.
Avoid foods you dislike (fried, spicy) and focus on foods you love (chicken, paneer, egg) prepared in healthy ways.
